Listing Installed Programs
To list all the installed programs, you can use a PowerShell command to show
the contents of the Program Files and Program Files (x86) folders. (The list of
applications will allow us to spot any old software installed that we can exploit.)
PS C:\Users\Gus> Get-ChildItem 'C:\Program Files', 'C:\Program Files (x86)' |

Listing Tasks and Processes
To list all the tasks and processes on the Windows OS, you will need to use the
tasklist /v command. The output of this command is big and cumbersome.
You can filter the results to show only the system processes:

To list the scheduled tasks on the host, you can use the PowerShell command
to get the results. In the following command, we’re using a filter to exclude the
tasks related to Microsoft, since we’re interested in the custom scheduled tasks:
PS C:\Users\Gus> Get-ScheduledTask | where {$_.TaskPath -notlike "\Microsoft*"}
| ft TaskName,TaskPath,State
